title: The Young Storekeeper
content: When Abraham Lincoln was a young man, he worked as a storekeeper in a small village. He was honest and fair in all his dealings. One day, a woman bought some goods and paid for them. After she left, Lincoln counted the money again and found that he had charged her six cents too much. He closed the store and walked three miles that evening to return the six cents to the woman. Another time, he weighed some tea for a customer and later discovered that he had given her less than she had paid for. He traveled a long distance to make it right. Lincoln's honesty became well known in the community. People trusted him because they knew he would never cheat them. This honesty was the foundation of his character, and it would later make him one of the most respected presidents in American history. He never forgot the lessons he learned as a young storekeeper: that a person's word is their bond, and that even small acts of honesty matter greatly.

title: The Story of William Tell
content: William Tell was a skilled archer and a brave man who lived in Switzerland. At that time, a cruel governor ruled the land. The governor placed his hat on a pole in the town square and ordered everyone to bow to it as a sign of respect. Tell refused to bow, so the governor arrested him and his son. The governor knew of Tell's skill with a bow and devised a cruel punishment. He ordered Tell to shoot an apple off his own son's head with a single arrow. Tell took two arrows from his quiver and placed one in his bow. He aimed carefully and shot the apple cleanly off his son's head without harming the boy. The governor was amazed, but then he asked about the second arrow. Tell replied that if he had missed and hit his son, he would have used the second arrow to kill the governor. The governor became angry and had Tell thrown into prison. Later, Tell escaped and eventually killed the governor, winning freedom for his people. This story is remembered as a symbol of courage and the fight for liberty.

title: Grace Darling
content: Grace Darling was the daughter of a lighthouse keeper on the Farne Islands off the coast of England. One stormy night in September 1838, Grace looked out from the lighthouse and saw a ship wrecked on the rocks in the raging sea. The storm was fierce, with howling winds and crashing waves, but Grace was determined to help. She pleaded with her father to take their small boat out to rescue the survivors. Her father hesitated, but Grace insisted. They rowed through the dangerous waters, fighting against the wind and currents. When they reached the wrecked ship, they found nine survivors clinging to the rocks. Grace guided them into the boat while her father held it steady. She rowed back to the lighthouse with the survivors, saving their lives. Grace Darling became a national heroine. Her courage and compassion were celebrated across the country. She never sought fame, but her act of bravery inspired many and is still remembered today.

title: Robin Hood and Little John
content: Robin Hood was an outlaw who lived in Sherwood Forest with his band of Merry Men. He robbed from the rich and gave to the poor. One day, he came across a tall stranger on a narrow bridge over a river. Robin refused to let the stranger pass without a fight. The stranger was Little John, and he was nearly seven feet tall. They fought with quarterstaffs, and Robin was knocked into the water. Robin laughed and asked the stranger to join his band. Little John agreed and became Robin's most trusted friend. They had many adventures together, robbing from greedy nobles and helping the poor. The Sheriff of Nottingham often tried to capture Robin, but he always failed. Robin Hood and his men lived as outlaws in the forest, but they were heroes to the common people. Their story has been told for centuries as a tale of justice and friendship.

title: Robert Bruce and the Spider
content: Robert Bruce was the King of Scotland. He fought bravely to win freedom for his country, but he was defeated in battle six times. After his sixth defeat, he hid in a cave to escape from his enemies. He was discouraged and felt like giving up. As he sat there, he watched a spider trying to spin its web. The spider tried to swing from one beam to another, but it failed. It tried again and again, six times, and each time it fell. On the seventh attempt, the spider swung across and succeeded. Bruce watched this and thought about his own life. If the spider could keep trying after six failures, then so could he. He left the cave and gathered his men. They fought a seventh battle, and this time they won. Robert Bruce became the King of a free Scotland. He never forgot the lesson of the spider: that perseverance can turn failure into success.

title: Dry Rain and the Hatchet
content: There was once an Indian chief named Dry Rain. He was known for his wisdom and honesty. One day, he traded his furs with a white trader for some goods. When he returned to his village, he discovered that the trader had given him an extra hatchet by mistake. Dry Rain's heart was troubled. He heard two voices in his heart: one said to keep the hatchet and that it was good luck, the other said to return it. He thought about it through the night. In the morning, Dry Rain got up early and walked for two days to return the hatchet to the trader. He said to the trader: I could not sleep with a theft in my heart. The trader was deeply impressed by Dry Rain's honesty and told many others about his good character. Dry Rain became known as a man who would not take what was not his, and the story of his honesty was passed down for generations among both the Indian and white people.

title: The Trojan Horse
content: The Greeks and the Trojans had been at war for ten years. The Greeks had tried many times to capture the city of Troy, but its walls were too strong. One day, the Greeks built a giant wooden horse and hid their best soldiers inside it. They left it outside the gates of Troy and pretended to sail away. The Trojans were delighted to see them go and thought the horse was a gift. They argued about what to do with it, but decided to bring it into the city. A Greek spy named Sinon warned them not to trust the horse. He said it would bring disaster. The Trojans ignored him. That night, while the Trojans were sleeping, the Greek soldiers came out of the horse and opened the city gates. The Greek army, which had returned by night, rushed in and destroyed Troy. The wooden horse became famous as the trick that finally ended the long war. This story shows that even the strongest defenses can be broken with clever thinking.

title: The Sword of Damocles
content: There was once a king named Dionysius who ruled over a rich and powerful kingdom. His friend Damocles often praised him for his happiness and good fortune. Damocles said that the king must be the happiest man alive because he had wealth, power, and everything he could desire. The king decided to teach Damocles a lesson. He offered to swap places with him for a day. Damocles was thrilled. He sat on the royal throne, wore the king's robes, and ate the finest food. But just above his head, the king had hung a sharp sword, held by a single thread of horsehair. Damocles looked up and saw the sword dangling over him. His joy turned to fear. He could not enjoy the feast because he was afraid that at any moment the sword would fall and kill him. He begged the king to let him go. The king smiled and said: This is the true nature of power. No one is truly safe when they sit at the top. Damocles understood that the king's life was not as happy as it seemed.

title: The Brave Little Tailor
content: A tailor was sewing one day when a swarm of flies landed on his bread and jam. He swatted them and killed seven with one blow. He was so proud that he made a belt with the words Seven in One Blow and set out to see the world. He met a giant who did not believe his boast. The tailor challenged the giant to prove his strength. He squeezed water from a stone, which was actually a piece of cheese in his pocket. He threw a bird into the air and told the giant to bring it back, but the bird flew away. The tailor married the princess and became a king. He had many adventures along the way and faced many challenges. He solved the riddle of the unicorn and the wild boar. The brave little tailor taught everyone that courage and cleverness are more important than size. A man with a quick mind can defeat even the strongest opponent.

title: The Argonauts and the Golden Fleece
content: Jason was a young prince who wanted to reclaim his kingdom. His wicked uncle, King Pelias, told him he would give back the kingdom if Jason could bring him the Golden Fleece. The fleece was guarded by a fierce dragon and was kept far away in the land of Colchis. Jason gathered a band of heroes called the Argonauts and built a ship called the Argo. They sailed through many dangers, facing terrible storms and fighting against giants. They passed through the Clashing Rocks, where two cliffs crashed together and crushed ships between them. When they arrived in Colchis, the king set impossible tasks for Jason to complete before he could take the fleece. With the help of the king's daughter, Medea, Jason was able to complete the tasks and steal the fleece from the dragon. They sailed back home, but the journey was long and full of trials. Jason's adventure became one of the greatest stories in Greek mythology.

title: The Gift of the Magi
content: Della and Jim were a young couple who loved each other dearly. They were very poor, and Christmas was approaching. Della wanted to buy a special gift for Jim but had almost no money. She sold her beautiful long hair to buy a platinum chain for Jim's prized possession, a gold watch that had belonged to his father. When Jim came home that evening and saw Della's short hair, he was shocked. Della tried to explain that she had sold her hair to buy him a gift. Then Della gave Jim the chain she had bought. But Jim had sold his watch to buy a set of beautiful combs for Della's long hair. They both realized that their gifts had become useless, but they also realized that they had given the greatest gift of all: their love for each other. Their love was worth more than any material possession. This story reminds us that the true meaning of giving lies in sacrifice and love.

title: The Last Lesson
content: It was the last day of school in the French district of Alsace. The Germans had won the war and French was no longer allowed to be taught in the schools. The new master would come tomorrow to teach German. M. Hamel, the old teacher, stood before the class in his best clothes. He told the students that this was their last French lesson, and that they must never forget their language. He said: A people who hold onto their language hold onto their freedom. The students worked harder than they ever had before. They realized that they had taken their language and their education for granted. The class listened to the sound of the church bells ringing for the last time in French. M. Hamel wrote Vive la France on the blackboard. When the lesson was finished, he turned and dismissed the class. The students left knowing they had lost something precious.

title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
content: Ichabod Crane was a lanky schoolmaster who came to the quiet Dutch village of Sleepy Hollow. He was superstitious and loved to listen to old ghost stories, especially the tale of the Headless Horseman, a ghost who rode through the night in search of his missing head. Ichabod fell in love with Katrina, the daughter of a wealthy farmer. But he had a rival named Brom Bones, who was strong and popular. After a party at Katrina's house, Ichabod rode home in the dark, feeling uneasy. As he passed the old church, he saw a large figure on horseback with no head. It was the Headless Horseman! Ichabod fled in terror, but the horseman threw his head at him. Ichabod was never seen again. The village people said the Headless Horseman took him away. Only his trampled hat and a shattered pumpkin were found. Ichabod's disappearance remains a mystery to this day.

title: The Necklace
content: Mathilde was a beautiful young woman who dreamed of a life of wealth and luxury. She was married to a poor clerk and felt unhappy with her simple life. One day, she was invited to a grand ball. She borrowed a beautiful diamond necklace from her rich friend. At the ball, she looked stunning and was the envy of every woman there. When she returned home, she discovered that the necklace was gone. She and her husband searched everywhere but could not find it. They bought a replacement necklace for a huge sum of money, but they had to borrow heavily to afford it. For the next ten years, they lived in poverty, working hard to pay off the debt. Mathilde lost all her beauty and became old and tired. One day, she met her friend and told her the whole story. Her friend said: My necklace was not real, it was only made of imitation diamonds! The loss was meaningless. Mathilde understood the terrible cost of her pride.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo (Excerpt)
content: Edmond Dantès was a young sailor who had everything: a good job, a loving father, and a beautiful fiancée named Mercédès. He was framed by his jealous rivals and imprisoned in the Château d'If, a dark and terrible prison on an island. He spent fourteen years in that prison. During his imprisonment, he met an old priest named Abbé Faria, who taught him many things and revealed the location of a vast treasure on the island of Monte Cristo. Dantès escaped and found the treasure. He then began a long and careful plan to punish those who had betrayed him. He sent his enemies a letter that read: I am the one whom you have dishonored. I am the one whom you killed. He found power and wealth through the treasure. His thirst for revenge drove him to become the Count of Monte Cristo. He punished his enemies and rewarded those who had helped him. He learned that the true value of life lies not in revenge but in forgiveness.
